outcome: HYV area grew from 1.9m ha (FY1960) to 15.4m (1970), 43.1m (1980) and 63.9m ha (1990). By FY1980, 75% of wheat area and 45% of rice area used HYVs. Gains concentrated where water was assured; poverty fell faster in high-yield states.
theme: Green Revolution (HYV seeds + fertilizer + irrigation + credit + price support)
transferability: High for the input bundle and sequencing (start in high-potential irrigated zones). Medium overall, because Africa's crop diversity, rain-fed systems and soil heterogeneity need many crop-specific varieties, and the groundwater depletion and fertilizer-subsidy fiscal burden should be avoided.
what_happened: From the mid-1960s India bundled Mexican/Philippine HYV wheat and rice with assured irrigation, subsidized fertilizer, farm credit and procurement prices, starting in Punjab, Haryana and western UP.

outcome: 24.07bn transactions worth Rs 29.37 lakh crore in Sept 2026 (~802m a day); 218.6bn transactions in FY26. Rails enable direct benefit transfers and digital credit for farmers.
theme: Digital public infrastructure: UPI (India Stack)
transferability: High: Africa already leads in mobile money. The gap is interoperability and open ID/registries; PAPSS and national instant-payment systems (Ethiopia, Nigeria NIP, Ghana GhIPSS) can copy the open-API model.
what_happened: Interoperable real-time payment rails (UPI, 2016) on top of Aadhaar ID and Jan Dhan accounts, run by NPCI as a public-private utility with zero merchant fees.

outcome: Over Rs 4.27 lakh crore transferred to 9.32 crore (93m) farmers, including 2.15 crore women, by March 2026 (22nd installment Rs 18,640 crore).
theme: PM-KISAN direct benefit transfer to farmers
transferability: Medium: delivery rails (ID + registry + payments) are highly transferable for e-voucher input subsidies (Nigeria, Zambia e-FISP, Malawi). Universal cash at this scale is fiscally hard for most African budgets.
what_happened: Since 2019, unconditional Rs 6,000/yr income support paid in three installments by DBT to Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts.

outcome: 1,656 mandis integrated, 1.80 crore farmers, 2.73 lakh traders and 4,724 FPOs registered; cumulative trade of 13.25 crore t worth Rs 4.84 lakh crore over 10 years (to Mar 2026). Inter-state trade adoption has stayed modest.
theme: e-NAM national electronic agricultural market
transferability: Medium: commodity exchanges (Ethiopia ECX, Ghana GCX, Malawi AHCX) show demand, but success depends on assaying, warehousing and trader buy-in. Within AfCFTA, regional e-markets could link surplus and deficit zones.
what_happened: Launched 2016 to link physical APMC mandis on an online trading platform with e-auctions, assaying and online payment.

outcome: 11 crore (110m) farmer IDs generated by Oct 2026, five months ahead of the March 2027 deadline.
theme: Digital Agriculture Mission / AgriStack (farmer ID, crop survey, geo-referenced land registry)
transferability: High: the clearest template for African farmer registries (Kenya KIAMIS, Ethiopia, Rwanda, Nigeria). Requires land-record digitization and data protection consistent with the AU Data Policy Framework.
what_happened: Launched 2024: federated farmer registry linked to land records, digital crop survey and a geospatial village map. Used for credit, insurance, procurement and advisory.

outcome: Agricultural TFP grew ~3.08%/yr (1975-2016) and explained 80.6% of output growth. Output rose 3.82%/yr vs 0.72% for inputs (more than 4x output in 40 years). Crop area went from 36.8m to 69.5m ha while pasture shrank. Embrapa's budget was R$3.4bn in 2017.
theme: Embrapa and the Cerrado transformation
transferability: High for Africa's acidic savanna zones and for a well-funded, autonomous national research corporation. Watch out for deforestation and land-concentration trade-offs.
what_happened: Embrapa (founded 1973) and universities developed liming and soil correction, tropical soybean varieties, biological N-fixation and no-till for the acidic Cerrado savanna. Combined with credit and infrastructure, this opened the Midwest to double-cropping.

outcome: 2025/26: R$516.2bn for commercial agriculture (R$414.7bn operating/commercialization, R$101.5bn investment) at 8.5-14% interest, plus R$78.2bn for family farming.
theme: Plano Safra: annual subsidized rural credit plan
transferability: Medium: Africa lacks the fiscal space for interest equalization at this scale, but the predictable annual credit envelope, the CPR (a tradable farm-receivable instrument) and bank lending mandates are transferable.
what_happened: A predictable annual plan sets volumes and interest-rate tiers for rural credit (operating, commercialization, investment), with separate lines for family farmers (Pronaf) and links to rural product certificates (CPR/LCA).

outcome: Leading farmers went from 67.9% to 97% of attainable yield; the county average rose from 62.8% to 79.6% (published in Nature, 2016).
theme: Science and Technology Backyards (participatory extension)
transferability: High: low-cost, university-anchored model that suits African universities and national research systems; could be combined with the youth agripreneur programs.
what_happened: China Agricultural University placed graduate students to live in villages (from Quzhou County, 2009), co-designing practices with farmers and forming quasi-cooperatives of 30-40 households.

outcome: From 20 Taobao villages in 2013 to 5,425 in 2020, with ~RMB 1 trillion in annual revenue.
theme: Rural e-commerce (Taobao villages)
transferability: Medium: Africa's last-mile logistics, payments and connectivity usage gaps are binding constraints; social commerce (WhatsApp/TikTok) and agent networks are the more likely path.
what_happened: Alibaba's platform plus government rural logistics and broadband drove clusters of village online shops selling farm products and crafts; Rural Taobao service centers acted as agents.

outcome: Shenzhen GDP went from RMB 270m (1980) to RMB 3.68 trillion (2024), more than a 10,000x increase in nominal terms.
theme: Special Economic Zones and infrastructure-led industrialization (Shenzhen)
transferability: Medium: many African SEZs underperform. Success needs reliable power, ports, one-stop administration and anchor investors. The AU Niamey 2022 decisions and AfDB SAPZs explicitly borrow the model (see Ethiopia's Hawassa and Benin's GDIZ).
what_happened: From 1980, SEZs offered regulatory autonomy, export processing, FDI incentives and dense infrastructure, close to Hong Kong capital and know-how.

outcome: Vietnam went from rice importer to the world's 2nd-3rd largest exporter. In 2024 it exported a record ~9 Mt worth US$5.7bn (prices above US$600/t). It is also a top coffee exporter.
theme: Doi Moi land reform and the rise of rice exports
transferability: High: shows that tenure security plus market freedom can unlock smallholder output fast. Relevant to African land reform (Ethiopia, Rwanda certification) and export crop strategies.
what_happened: Doi Moi (1986), Resolution 10 (1988) gave households production rights and the right to sell output. The 1993 Land Law granted 20-50 year tradable, mortgageable land-use rights. Followed by liberalized trade and investment in Mekong Delta irrigation.

outcome: Close to 100% of sewage is reused, and ~90% of treated wastewater goes to agriculture (Mekorot).
theme: Drip irrigation and wastewater reuse
transferability: Medium: drip and fertigation suit high-value horticulture in water-scarce North/East/Southern Africa. Capex, power, and water-pricing reforms limit transfer to staples.
what_happened: National water pricing and allocation, commercialization of drip irrigation (Netafim and others), desalination, and near-total sewage treatment and reuse for agriculture.

outcome: World's 2nd-largest food exporter by value. Greenhouse tomatoes need under 4 gallons of water per kg vs 16 in open fields. Potato yields exceed 20 t/acre vs ~9 global.
theme: Wageningen 'golden triangle' and greenhouse productivity
transferability: Medium: the triple-helix model and horticulture export clusters are relevant (Kenya flowers, Ethiopia/Morocco greenhouses). High-tech greenhouses are capital- and energy-intensive.
what_happened: Tight government-university-industry collaboration (Wageningen University & Research, Food Valley), controlled-environment horticulture, and logistics hubs (Rotterdam, Schiphol).

outcome: The 8028 hotline logged ~6.5m calls and 1m+ registered users within a year (730k farmers). Wheat area in the irrigated lowlands expanded from ~20,000 ha (2020) to over 500,000 ha in two years.
theme: Agricultural Transformation Agency (ATA/ATI) delivery unit and irrigated wheat
transferability: High: a peer African case of a presidential-level delivery unit (now copied in Rwanda, Nigeria, Tanzania) and IVR-based advisory at scale.
what_happened: ATA (2010), modeled on Asian (Korea, Taiwan, Malaysia) delivery units, ran the 8028 farmer hotline, soil mapping (EthioSIS), blended fertilizer and cluster farming. From 2020 the government pushed lowland irrigated wheat with ICARDA/AfDB TAAT.

outcome: 550,000+ power tillers prepare more than 80% of cropland. 72% of farmers use tillers and 66% use pumps through fee-for-service. Shallow tubewells grew from 93,000 (1982) to 260,000 (1990), driving near rice self-sufficiency.
theme: Small-machine mechanization and irrigation service markets
transferability: High: directly relevant to African smallholders under 2 ha. Lower import duties and standards on small machines, plus service-provider models, are low-cost policy levers.
what_happened: Liberalized import of Chinese power tillers and small diesel pumps (late 1980s), removal of standardization barriers, and emergence of fee-for-service rental markets.

outcome: Output went from ~12 Mt (1968) to 39 Mt (1985), when self-sufficiency was reached; HYV adoption rose from 50% to 85%. In 2025, output of 34.71 Mt (+13.4%) gave a 3.52 Mt surplus with no consumption imports, and Bulog stocks peaked at a record 4.2 Mt.
theme: Rice self-sufficiency via BIMAS and Bulog buffer stocks
transferability: Medium: shows the power of a coherent input + irrigation + price policy package. Fiscal costs and the pesticide/planthopper lesson (IPM adopted 1988) matter; Nigeria and Senegal rice strategies are analogues.
what_happened: BIMAS 'mass guidance' bundled HYV seed, subsidized fertilizer, credit and extension. The state rehabilitated 2.5m ha of irrigation, and Bulog managed price-stabilizing buffer stocks. Renewed in 2025 with an import halt.

outcome: 2024 revenue of MAD 97bn (~US$10bn), with fertilizers 69% of revenue (66% in 2023). Second phase of the investment program is under way.
theme: OCP phosphate value addition: from rock to tailored fertilizers
transferability: High for resource-rich states (Nigeria gas-to-urea, Ethiopia potash, Tanzania gas, Togo/Senegal phosphate). Shows that keeping value in Africa needs scale, a state champion and market development.
what_happened: The state-owned OCP shifted from exporting phosphate rock to fertilizers and acids, invested in integrated hubs (Jorf Lasfar), and created OCP Africa with soil mapping and customized blends for African markets.

outcome: 100+ land-grant institutions. Built the integrated research-education-extension model behind long-run US farm productivity growth.
theme: Land-grant universities and cooperative extension
transferability: High in design: Africa's agricultural universities are rarely mandated or funded for extension. Linking universities, research institutes and county extension is a low-regret reform.
what_happened: The Morrill Act (1862) funded agricultural colleges, the Hatch Act (1887) created experiment stations, and the Smith-Lever Act (1914) created the cooperative extension system linking research to farms.

outcome: €263bn EU funds (€307bn with national co-financing). About €98bn (~32%) goes to climate/environment actions, €8.5bn to young farmers (377,000 expected), and ~15% of farmers get risk-management support. All 28 plans were approved.
theme: CAP 2023-2027 reform: green conditionality and strategic plans
transferability: Medium: Africa cannot match subsidy levels, but results-based national plans (as CAADP NAIPs aim to be), youth entry incentives and subsidized risk tools are instructive. EU deforestation and CBAM rules also affect African exporters.
what_happened: Moved to national CAP Strategic Plans with performance targets. Eco-schemes take ~24% of direct payments, and payments are linked to environmental (and for the first time social/labour) conditions.

outcome: Farmer.Chat served 15,000+ users and 300,000+ queries across Kenya (225,500 queries), India, Nigeria and Ethiopia, answering ~75% of questions. Earlier video-based extension cut cost per adoption from US$35 to US$3.50.
theme: 2024-2026 trend: generative AI agricultural advisory
transferability: High: addresses Africa's 1:2,000-1:10,000 extension ratios. Needs local-language data, content governance, and voice/IVR for low-literacy farmers.
what_happened: LLM-based advisors (Digital Green's Farmer.Chat, India's Kisan e-Mitra and AgriStack-linked AI) deliver voice/text advice in local languages, grounded in vetted extension content.

outcome: Ghana became the 4th African country with guidelines (2023), creating faster paths for drought- and disease-resistant crops.
theme: 2022-2026 trend: gene-editing regulation that separates SDN-1/2 edits from GMOs
transferability: High: low-cost regulatory reform. Regional harmonization via RECs would create larger markets for African breeders.
what_happened: Nigeria, Kenya (Feb 2022), Malawi and Ghana (Nov 2023) issued genome-editing guidelines allowing case-by-case determination that edits without foreign DNA are not regulated as GMOs. Supported by AUDA-NEPAD ABNE.

outcome: In March 2025 AgriCarbon issued 39,207 t of credits from 17,582 ha across 29 farms.
theme: 2024-2026 trend: carbon markets and regenerative agriculture (Verra VM0042)
transferability: Medium: MRV costs and price volatility make smallholder carbon hard. Aggregation, remote sensing and Article 6 frameworks are improving the economics; best as a co-benefit, not a core revenue.
what_happened: Soil-carbon methodologies (Verra VM0042) now issue credits for regenerative practices. South Africa's AgriCarbon was the first in Africa and second globally under VM0042.

outcome: Global agricultural biologicals market estimated at US$15.1bn (2024), US$17.2bn (2025), projected US$43.6bn by 2032 (~14% CAGR).
theme: 2024-2026 trend: agricultural biologicals (biofertilizers, biostimulants, biopesticides)
transferability: High: local production of rhizobia inoculants and biopesticides is low-capex and fits the AU Soil Health plan's 'organic and inorganic' approach. Needs registration pathways and quality control.
what_happened: Fast growth of microbial and biological inputs as a complement to synthetic fertilizer and pesticides, driven by soil health goals and EU pesticide restrictions.

outcome: Indian exports fell from 21.3 to 14.3 Mt. Thai 5% prices were ~20% above pre-ban levels. Indian rice exports to Africa fell 43% (~5.3 Mt), and SSA consumers paid an estimated ~US$3.8bn extra. Indian rice was more than 60% of rice imports for 17 African countries.
theme: 2022-2024 trend: food export bans and import dependence
transferability: High as a lesson: argues for regional strategic reserves, AfCFTA staple trade and domestic rice/wheat productivity (the Kampala target to triple intra-African agrifood trade).
what_happened: India restricted rice exports (broken rice ban Sept 2022; non-basmati white rice ban July 2023), lifting most curbs in Sept-Oct 2024.
